challenges.title: Challenges we address
challenges.intro: A low-carbon transition is rarely blocked by a lack of green technology. It is blocked by access, data, skills, financing and proof of results.

items.title: Greenwashing and unverifiable claims
items.problem: Environmental statements that cannot be checked erode the trust of buyers, banks and investors.
items.response: Trusted data, transparency and measurement, reporting and verification (MRV).

items.title: Fragmented, incomplete data
items.problem: Energy, production, supply chain and waste data sit in invoices, spreadsheets and people's heads.
items.response: GP.A turns conversations, documents, photos and voice into structured data and pre-fills your reporting tools.

items.title: Regulation that is hard to apply
items.problem: International regulations, reporting duties and EPR obligations arrive faster than businesses can interpret them.
items.response: Compliance support and EPR implementation, aligned with the frameworks your buyers and regulators use.

items.title: Limited access to technology for SMEs
items.problem: Enterprise-grade tools are too costly, too complex or too hard to integrate.
items.response: Drop-in solutions that plug into your existing operations and tools, only when you need them.

items.title: Missing technical and strategic skills
items.problem: Teams lack the time and expertise to build a climate strategy while running daily operations.
items.response: Business capacity building: step-by-step guidance, action plans and peer learning.

items.title: Financing the transition
items.problem: Banks and investors ask for green documentation that most SMEs do not have.
items.response: Green finance readiness: eligibility scoring, gaps, a roadmap and investor-grade climate data.

items.title: Resistance to change
items.problem: Teams and managers hesitate to change habits without visible, short-term progress.
items.response: Behaviour change and business engagement through short milestones, each shown as a live progress dial.

items.title: From pilot to deployment
items.problem: Good pilot projects stall before they scale across sites, products or suppliers.
items.response: Implementation support to scale and expand what works.

whyNow.title: Why now: four forces converging on businesses
whyNow.subtitle: Some are immediate and binding. Others build pressure over time. GP.A addresses each one, starting where the need is most urgent.

forces.title: International regulations
forces.changing: Export markets are tightening carbon and supply chain disclosure requirements for the goods they import.
forces.impact: Exporters must supply verified emissions data or risk losing contracts and market access.
forces.response: Export readiness assessment and structured data for your reporting software (ESG, audit and official reports).

forces.title: Reporting cascade
forces.changing: Large companies and regulated sectors now have to publish official reports (ESG, audit, emissions).
forces.impact: They press their SME suppliers for emissions data those suppliers have never tracked.
forces.response: Guided data collection so suppliers can answer buyer requests with credible numbers.

forces.title: Green credit pressure
forces.changing: Banks are expanding their green credit guidelines.
forces.impact: Green documentation is increasingly a gate to financing, not just a bonus, even outside regulated sectors.
forces.response: Green loan eligibility scoring, gaps, a roadmap and an estimated readiness timeline.

forces.title: Wider carbon-market scope
forces.changing: Carbon pricing and trading schemes are expanding in phases toward economy-wide coverage.
forces.impact: Sectors and company sizes not covered today will come into scope, with little warning.
forces.response: Businesses that start structuring their data now will already be prepared when the scope widens.

vietstock.title: "Greenwashing" from the perspective of an international ESG consultant
vietstock.quote: Recently, we have been testing an application called GreenPulse.AI. This is an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant that helps SMEs in Vietnam and Southeast Asia easily practice sustainability. Users will be guided step-by-step to solve issues such as reducing electricity costs, meeting export requirements, with a dashboard to track progress. The platform also integrates automatic ESG reporting tools according to international standards. The main purpose is to help businesses avoid the 'greenwashing' trap, demonstrate measurable improvements, and expand access to investors, customers and international markets.

questions.question: How is GreenPulse different from ChatGPT or other general AI tools?
questions.answer: GP.A is built for climate and sustainability work. It is guided by international standards (ISO, ESG and audit reporting) and by local regulation, and it connects to your own data sources. It produces structured outputs that feed your reporting tools, not generic text that needs manual review.

questions.question: Is my data secure? Do you share it with third parties?
questions.answer: FREE PLAN: your conversations use third-party AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic). Data is transmitted to their servers (US-based) for processing. These providers may use conversation data for model improvement unless opted-out. PREMIUM & PRO PLANS (coming soon): we plan to offer locally-hosted AI models (Llama 3) deployed in Southeast Asia, so that your data stays within our infrastructure, with no third-party sharing and in line with local data residency requirements. All data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and at rest (AES-256).

questions.question: Do you replace a certifying body or an auditor?
questions.answer: No. GP.A structures your evidence file, identifies gaps and prepares you for eco-labels, ISO and export standards. The certifying authority and any independent verifier keep their role.

questions.question: Doesn't AI generate emissions? How do you manage this?
questions.answer: Yes, AI computing does generate emissions, which is why we keep our own footprint in check. GreenPulse's automation also aims to reduce travel, paper reports and redundant manual work for our users.

questions.question: Can GreenPulse integrate with our existing tools?
questions.answer: Yes. GP.A drops into your existing operations: it connects with major ERP systems (SAP, Oracle), CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot), and data sources (Excel, Google Sheets, CSV). Specialist tools for certification, reporting or traceability are plugged in only when your goal calls for them. Our API allows custom integrations for proprietary systems. Most implementations are live within 2 weeks.

questions.question: What if GreenPulse makes a mistake in compliance reporting?
questions.answer: GreenPulse provides transparency in all outputs, showing which frameworks and data points inform each recommendation. All reports include human-in-the-loop review checkpoints before finalization. We also offer audit trails and version control to ensure regulatory confidence.
